modules.name: leave-type
owns: LeaveType enum (annual, sick, emergency, unpaid, maternity, paternity)

modules.name: leave-status
owns: LeaveStatus enum (DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED)

recommended_phases.title: Phase 1: Foundation — Enums, Audit, and Employee
recommended_phases.rationale: Leaf modules with zero internal dependencies. leave-type and leave-status are pure enums. audit-log is the cross-cutting audit service required by GP-002. employee provides identity and manager hierarchy needed by all downstream modules. These must exist before anything else.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2: Policy and Notification
recommended_phases.rationale: leave-policy depends only on leave-type and audit-log (both in Phase 1). notification depends only on employee (Phase 1). These are independent of each other and can be built in parallel, but both are prerequisites for leave-balance and leave-request.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3: Leave Balance
recommended_phases.rationale: leave-balance depends on leave-policy (Phase 2), employee (Phase 1), and audit-log (Phase 1). It provides the balance tracking, deduction, and restoration that leave-request needs for validation and lifecycle management.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4: Leave Request — Core Application Logic
recommended_phases.rationale: leave-request is the orchestrating module that depends on every other module. It wires together policy validation, balance checks, manager approval routing, audit recording, and notification dispatch. Building it last ensures all dependencies are stable.

app_notes:
## Layer Boundaries

- **Domain layer** (innermost): `leave-type`, `leave-status` — pure enums and value objects with no dependencies.
- **Infrastructure layer**: `audit-log` — cross-cutting audit service (GP-002). `employee` — identity and org-hierarchy data access.
- **Domain services**: `leave-policy`, `leave-balance` — business rules for policy lookup and balance arithmetic.
- **Application layer** (outermost): `leave-request` — orchestrates the full leave lifecycle: validates policy, checks balance, routes to manager, records audit, dispatches notifications.

## Dependency Direction (verified acyclic)

```
leave-request ──→ leave-balance ──→ leave-policy ──→ leave-type
    │                 │                  │
    │                 │                  └──→ audit-log
    │                 │
    │                 └──→ employee ──→ audit-log
    │
    ├──→ leave-status (leaf)
    ├──→ notification ──→ employee
    └──→ audit-log (leaf)
```

## Key Design Decisions

- **LeaveRequestService is the sole orchestrator**: it calls `ILeaveBalanceService.hasSufficientBalance`, `ILeavePolicyService.validatePolicyForLeaveType`, `IEmployeeService.getManagerForEmployee`, `IAuditService.recordApprove/recordReject`, and `INotificationService.notify*`. No other module orchestrates across domains.
- **Balance deduction happens on approval, not submission**: `approveLeaveRequest` calls `deductBalance`. `rejectLeaveRequest` and `cancelLeaveRequest` call `restoreBalance` only if previously approved.
- **Status transitions are enforced in leave-status**: DRAFT→SUBMITTED→(APPROVED|REJECTED); APPROVED→CANCELLED. The leave-request service delegates to leave-status for valid transition checks.
- **RBAC (GP-005) is enforced at the controller/route layer**: the leave-request controller checks that the caller is the employee (for submit/cancel) or the manager (for approve/reject) before delegating to the service.
- **All state-changing operations produce audit records (GP-002)**: submit, approve, reject, cancel each write via IAuditService.
